_why: The citation ratchet, keyed by CONFIGURATION, because the checker does not measure the same
population in every configuration. With an ORCA checkout resolved, ~527 citations into ORCA's
tree are checked and ~129 paths are external; without one, those same paths fall to external
and the count is drawn from a partly DISJOINT set. A single number enforced across both is not
a threshold on anything: seven repairs moved the ORCA-resolved count 92 -> 85 and the
ORCA-absent count 98 -> 98, on the same pinned tree.
A number here is a RATCHET, not an amnesty. It may only go DOWN. Raising it to make a job
green is how a checker becomes decoration (PITFALLS P33). THE NUMBERS BELOW ARE NOT MET AT
HEAD AND HAVE DELIBERATELY NOT BEEN RAISED TO MEET IT — see `standing` vs `measured`.
Every reading was taken on a CLEAN DETACHED WORKTREE at the stated commit, with node_modules
symlinked in. A count taken in the shared working tree is not comparable: it reads whatever
five peers have uncommitted. The same tree read 139 while one peer had os-synth/index.ts open.

So the gate is red for CODE CHURN in a heavily-cited file, and it has no honest path to

superseded.gate on the total: Superseded 2026-08-21 by the move to LOST. See gateChangedWhy, quoteGoneDecision and unreadAnnotationDecision, which together record everything the gate does and does not cover.

gateChangedWhy: THE GATE WAS NARROWED ON PURPOSE, from the TOTAL stale count to LOST alone. Recorded here
rather than left to be discovered, because a quality gate that gets narrower without an
explanation is indistinguishable from one that was loosened to make a job green.
A stale citation is three different things: DRIFTED (the anchor is still in the cited file,
somewhere else - the claim is intact and the pointer is off), LOST (the anchor is nowhere in the
file - the claim itself is in question), and QUOTE-GONE (the document quotes code verbatim and
that code is gone - almost always a REMEDIED defect, never safe to re-point).
DRIFTED tracks CODE CHURN, not documentation decisions. Measured: 4ccfa20, a one-file bug fix in
os-synth, moved the ORCA-resolved total from 85 to 130 in a single commit with no documentation
changing at all - bisected in a pinned worktree, controlled by scoring the same tree 85 under the
old script and 85 under the new one. A gate on the total therefore punishes whoever fixes a bug
in a heavily-cited file and rewards leaving it alone.
And it had NO HONEST EXIT. Raising the number to 130 is decoration. Re-pointing the 66 rows in
006-fma is actively HARMFUL: that document is stale by remedy, so a re-pointed citation lands on
the fix while the sentence beside it describes the defect - a false claim, strictly worse than
the stale pointer it replaces. A gate whose only exits are 'lie' and 'make it worse' is broken.
LOST is churn-invariant. Only a decision about the documents can create one, a bug fix cannot,
and it is 1 today - so a ratchet of 1 is a bound that means something. DRIFTED and QUOTE-GONE are
still PRINTED ON EVERY RUN, side by side with LOST, so nothing is hidden; they simply stop
pretending to be a gate.
Authorised by the architect 2026-08-21 as a reversible, documented change to what the gate means.
THE STRONGER FIX IS ITS OWN JOB and deliberately not started: 004 Panel E's 'cite a symbol plus
the line', with the tool RESOLVING the line from the symbol rather than comparing against it. At
that point drift stops existing rather than being tolerated, and the DRIFTED bucket empties
instead of being excused. See docs/.research/citation-audit.md, 'What the ratchet should measure
instead'.

standing_total_stale_SUPERSEDED.why: The old TOTAL-count ratchet, measured clean at 98309f8, kept visible rather than deleted. It was never met again after 4ccfa20 and was never raised to meet it - see gateChangedWhy.

quoteGoneDecision: QUOTE-GONE IS REPORTED AND NOT GATED. The architect asked for the argument rather than a guess,
so here it is, and it turns on WHO CREATES ONE.
A new QUOTE-GONE appears when somebody FIXES CODE that a document quotes verbatim. That is the
same shape as the DRIFTED problem one level up: gating it makes the bug fix the thing that breaks
the build. The person who fixed the bug is usually not the person who can fix the document, and
for 006-fma fixing the document is not an edit at all - it is the pin-vs-reconcile decision that
belongs to the author. Blocking their commit leaves them a bad doc edit or a bypass, which is the
'lie or make it worse' trap the LOST move was made to escape.
Nor would a ratchet at the current count help. It may only fall, and the next good fix to quoted
code raises it - so it would go red for exactly the behaviour we want, and the only way back to
green would be to raise it. A ratchet that a correct action breaks is not a ratchet.
WHAT IS DIFFERENT FROM DRIFTED, AND WHY IT STILL PRINTS ITS ROWS. DRIFTED is a navigation problem:
the claim is intact, the pointer is off. QUOTE-GONE is a SEMANTIC divergence - the document
describes code that is no longer there - so it is worth acting on and worth naming row by row
with the vanished quote beside it. It is a work queue, not a gate. It is 19 today and none of them
can be cleared without a human reading the row.
REVISIT IT if QUOTE-GONE ever stops being dominated by 006. Today 15 of 19 are in the record
documents, where re-pointing is harmful by construction. If a future QUOTE-GONE population were
mostly live documents that CAN be fixed cheaply, gating it at a falling ratchet would become
reasonable, because then a correct action would clear it rather than break it.
unreadAnnotationDecision: MALFORMED citation-check MARKERS ARE GATED AT ZERO. PROSE STAMPS ARE REPORTED.
The architect's instinct was right and the split is what makes it actionable. A malformed marker
is a FALSE CLAIM OF COVERAGE: somebody wrote `<!-- citation-check: ignore - reason -->` intending
to suppress a check, the matcher accepts nothing between `ignore` and `-->`, and the suppression
never happened while the document reads as though it did. That is strictly worse than a stale
citation, which is wrong and says so. It has already done damage - `--fix` rewrote
plugin-host-api.ts:261-265, the one citation 009 E-01 says explicitly not to touch, because its
marker was one of these (PITFALLS P35).
Gated at ZERO, and the count is zero today. Zero is the only moment when setting a threshold is
not an argument about a backlog, which is the whole lesson of the 34.
A PROSE STAMP is not a claim about this tool. 017 writes `[live tree]` and states at its top that
those pointers may have moved; that is a disclosure addressed to a reader. Failing on it would
punish a document for being honest about its own volatility. Named, so the next person knows the
parser does not honour it, and not gated.
